question.text: Which of the following is the BEST LP-side negotiation tactic described in Chapter 6 for controlling the Fund's expense load?

answer.text: Demand that Fund Expenses be capped at a dollar number, then net-off such expenses against the Management Fee already paid to the IM
Require the Trustee to bear all fund operating costs
Request the GP to fund all expenses from sponsor commitment
Increase the Hurdle Rate to absorb expense drag

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6 explicitly states: 'The best-case scenario for investors would be to negotiate with the Investment Manager to net-off such expenses against the Management Fees, already being paid.' Coupled with an expense cap, this caps LP economics. The Trap: B misuses the trustee role (fixed fee-based oversight, not cost-absorbing); C is fanciful; D confuses hurdle with expense cap. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests LP-side negotiation. Management-fee offset is a market-standard ask, especially from anchor and cornerstone LPs. Manager's Pro-Tip: As GP, proactively offer a 100% management-fee offset against transaction fees you earn from portfolio cos (directors' fees, monitoring fees, break-up fees). LPs value this highly and it's worth more at fundraise time than the fees themselves.
